note.question: Can a supplier’s SR capability be credibly communicated through free and unverifiable self-reporting?
note.overview: To manage supplier social responsibility (SR), some firms have adopted a self-assessment strategy whereby they ask suppliers to self-report SR capabilities. Self-reported information is difficult to verify, and this leads to an important credibility question: can a buyer expect truthful reporting? The paper examines whether a supplier’s SR capability can be credibly communicated through free and unverifiable self-reporting.
